_why: One home for every version constraint in this suite. The templates and the canaries read this file rather than repeating a range, because a number written in two places is a number that will disagree with itself and no check will notice. tests/test_pins.py fails if any workflow hardcodes one. PUBLISH ORDER MATTERS: this manifest ships inside the wheel, so a floor naming a version that is not on the index yet is false for as long as that is true. Nothing here can check it -- that is a network question and this file deliberately asks none -- so publish every component a floor names BEFORE publishing this package. 0.1.0 shipped a manifest that was correct for ten minutes and cost a second release.

redfish-service-validator.role: DMTF's own schema conformance suite. Adopted, not built.

redfish-protocol-validator.role: DMTF's own protocol conformance suite. Adopted, not built.

bmc-sensor-audit.role: The referee: declaration diff, liveness, the walk. 0.3.3 is the floor since 2026-09-26, and it moved WITH the engine's range, as a pair, because the two cannot be chosen apart: 0.3.0 to 0.3.2 require arbiter-engine <0.2, and every release from 0.3.3 on requires it at 0.2.x. While this manifest admitted both halves beside an engine range of <0.2, the resolver could only ever install the older half -- measured by tools/probe_pin.py on 2026-09-26, every engine release the manifest admitted resolved this tool to 0.3.2, and 0.3.3, 0.3.4 and 0.3.5 did not resolve beside the rest of the manifest at all. Half the range was a claim no environment could hold, and every gate ran referee 0.3.2 on engine 0.1.18 while the index served 0.3.5 on 0.2.9. Nothing went red: the daily canaries read whatever resolved. The ceiling is still <0.4. 0.3.0 was the floor from 2026-09-09, when the ceiling moved to <0.4 and neither was guessed. The ceiling had to move because the certificate gate admits odm-cert-generator>=0.2.0, whose 0.2.2 requires this tool at >=0.3.0 -- so <0.3 asked for two things that cannot both hold, and pip resolved that by quietly giving the certificate gate a version older than the manifest admits. It was 0.3.0 rather than the old 0.2.5 because both ends of a range are a claim: the injection gate, both envelope seams and the coverage surface were re-derived at 0.3.0 and at 0.3.2 and behave identically, and 0.2.5 was never run. 0.2.5 was the floor before that: it reworded the finding a removed sensor produces, from the machine to the capture, and the orchestrator scenarios expect the new text. 0.2.0 before that: from it the tool refuses `--insecure` beside `--pin-sha256` or `--cafile` rather than running unverified, and it answers `--version`. The coverage gate needs `validate-walk` and `capture --print-digest`, which is why 0.1.1 was the floor before the security fix raised it -- and this line still named 0.1.1 afterwards.

presence-audit.role: The referee's neutral half: declaration against capture in three states, the model the engine reads, and the reader of the envelope it returns. Split out of bmc-sensor-audit at that tool's 0.3.0, which this manifest now admits -- so it arrives transitively as well, and this line said the opposite until the ceiling moved on 2026-09-09. The direct pin stays: the core-engine canary names this package itself, and a seam whose subject reaches an environment only through another package's dependency is a seam that disappears the day that package stops needing it. 0.1.13 is the floor since 2026-09-26, later the same day, and for the same kind of reason: the referee's 0.3.7 and the certificate generator's 0.2.5 both require it, because 0.1.13 is the release that names a finding's subject `point`. The ceiling is <0.3 so the core's 0.2.0, which removes the old names, can arrive once every referee this manifest admits has moved; the suite ran against a 0.2.0 build before the ceiling admitted it. 0.1.10 was the floor before that, raised by the referee pair rather than by anything this pipeline reads: every referee the manifest now admits requires presence-audit >=0.1.10 (0.3.5 >=0.1.11), so 0.1.3 to 0.1.9 could no longer be installed beside it, and a floor below the one the referee enforces is a claim about releases no environment can hold. 0.1.3 was the floor before that, and not as a preference: it is the first release to publish ENVELOPE_SCHEMA_VERSION and PROTOCOL_VERSION, and the core-engine canary compares the first of those against the engine's own stamp instead of against a number written into a workflow.

arbiter-engine.role: The invariant envelope the referee reasons with. 0.2.7 is the floor since 2026-09-26, and it is DERIVED from the referee, not chosen: it is the lowest engine any referee this manifest admits will install beside -- bmc-sensor-audit 0.3.3 requires >=0.2.7, and 0.3.4 onward >=0.2.9. This range read >=0.1.8,<0.2 until then, three referee releases after the referee moved to the 0.2 line, and pip answered the pair by installing the older referee: the shape the odm-cert-generator entry records, a ceiling left behind when a dependency moved. The 0.1.8 floor before that was derived from the referee's own Stage 2 canary: the referee's own Stage 2 canary fails 11 of its assertions on 0.1.6 and 2 on 0.1.7, and passes on 0.1.8. This manifest declared >=0.1.6 until 2026-08-24, so a reader pinning down for reproducibility would have got a referee that could not do its job, on the manifest's word that it could.

qa-orchestrator.role: Injects faults, drives captures, compares verdicts. 0.3.2 is the floor and not a preference: the scenarios it ships expect the referee's current wording, and 0.3.0 and 0.3.1 ship a sensor-removed scenario expecting text the referee changed at 0.2.5 -- so both fail against every referee this manifest now admits. 0.3.0 was the floor before that: from it the harness is domain-free -- tiers, verbs, referees and report shapes come from registries, and the BMC tool with its tiers and scenarios is a vertical loaded through an entry point. `qa_orchestrator.backends` went with that change, and this pipeline read it until 2026-09-05. This line said 0.1.1 while the requirement already said 0.2.0: two records of one fact, drifted, which is what this manifest exists to prevent.

odm-cert-generator.role: Renders the certificate and holds unit identity. Published as `odm-cert-generator`; the command it installs is `cert-generator`, because PyPI refuses that as a distribution name. THE FLOOR MOVED 0.2.0 -> 0.2.2 on 2026-09-14, and it moved because a probe said so rather than because anybody re-read this note. 0.2.0 and 0.2.1 require `bmc-sensor-audit<0.3`, and this manifest requires `>=0.3.0,<0.4` -- so the two releases at the bottom of the declared range could not be installed beside the rest of it at all, and pip answered with ResolutionImpossible. The range claimed four releases and three of the other six pins; it held for two. This is the SAME defect as the one the referee entry records, pointing the other way: that one was a ceiling left behind when a dependency moved, this one a floor left behind when the referee ceiling moved to <0.4. What 0.2.0 was the floor FOR is unchanged and still true: the certificate records `walk_digest_verified` -- whether it COMPUTED the handle from the walk or was merely handed one and checked nothing -- and only from 0.2.0 is that claim worth anything. The number is higher now for a second reason stacked on the first, not instead of it. Measured by `tools/probe_pin.py`, which installs every release each range admits alongside every other pin and reads the resolved versions back.
